newsitem.title: ZAMBIA: NORWAY RESUMES PROJECT AID TO ZAMBIA.
newsitem.headline: NORWAY RESUMES PROJECT AID TO ZAMBIA.

text.p: Norway has resumed project funding to Zambia after freezing aid to Lusaka in 1996 in protest against constitutional changes which barred some candidates from participating in general elections.

Norway's ambassador Jon Lomoy told Reuters his country would grant Zambia 240 million kroner ($35 million) in project aid in 1997, but would maintain a freeze on balance of payment support to force reform.
"Norway will provide a total of 240 million kroner in project assistance to Zambia this year," Lomoy said.
"However, no balance of payment support has been allocated to Zambia under Norway's 1997 budget," he added.

Western government, led by the United States, suspended aid to Zambia after its government approved changes to the constitution which saw former president Kenneth Kaunda barred from contesting the November poll, won by President Frederick Chiluba.

Analysts say most donors now appear willing to restore normal aid flows to Zambia after assurances by Chiluba that his government will address governance concerns and keep its structural adjustment programme on track.

Donors resumed dialogue with the Zambian government in April after a year-long break and are due to hold a Consultative Group meeting on July 9 to make aid pledges to Zambia, which is banking on donors to meet one third of its $1.1 billion budget for 1997.
Lomoy said donors were pleased with some actions the government towards reform, but were still worried about the lack of dialogue between the government and opposition parties.
"We commend the government for establishing a human rights commission and for assurances that it will not control the media, but this does not mean we are satisfied in all areas," Lomoy said.
"We underline the importance of internal political dialogue aimed at arriving at a broad consensus on the rules of the political game," he added.
Zambian opposition parties have boycotted three parliamentary by-elections this year to force the government to nullify the outcome of last year's national poll and create a new voters register.
Four opposition parties are challenging the outcome of the election, which they claim were rigged, through electoral petitions.
The opposition Zambia Democratic Congress, headed by former deputy minister Dean Mungomba, says it will resort to violence to unseat the Chiluba government.
